chunks: Say: 'I do not ask any compensation of you for it, nor am I a specious pretender.'

key_terms.الْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ: specious pretenders or those who feigners or those who assume false roles for gain

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'I do not ask any compensation of you' in Surah Sad?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the Prophet's (SAWW) absolute sincerity (sidq) and freedom from worldly ambition (istighna), affirming that his mission was purely for Allah's sake. It serves as a foundational proof for the concept of 'Ismah (infallibility) and purity of intent, distinguishing the Prophetic station from mere preachers seeking patronage. This clarity in motive reinforces the authenticity of the message and invites believers to accept it without suspicion of hidden agendas.
